messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - Serving cluster 'west-2-prod' experiencing RDMA packet loss + node-level container crashes. Trigger: 30% retransmit rate on ib0 across 3 nodes, multiple runtime CUDA OOMs. Pager at 2026-03-15T02:12:01Z
Tara (oncall): I’m on it. Seeing alerts for 3 serving pods in pod-group infer-pool-7 -> CrashLoopBackOff. Rolling errors: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED and kernel timeouts.
Alice (sre): Confirmed network retransmits on nodes gpu-43, gpu-44, gpu-45. If the fabric is dropping, KV-cache syncs could blow memory/cuda on restart.
Miguel (runtime): Logs show repeated kvcache reconnects and then huge model load restarts. Snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T02:10:50Z] serve: reconnecting kvcache to peer gpu-44
[2026-03-15T02:11:02Z] runtime ERROR: CUDA OOM while allocating 11.2GB for qkv cache
[2026-03-15T02:11:03Z] containerd: killing process pid=3211 (OOM)
```
Tara (oncall): Are we seeing packet-loss only on IB or any ethernet too?
Ben (neteng): Early telemetry: IB path counters show retransmit surge on the fabric between rack-b and rack-c, ECN spikes and S/R timeouts. Ethernet lanes are fine. Looks like an IB link flapping due to MM config mismatch on one switch.
Jules (support): Is there customer impact? Any 5xx’s reported from apps? I'm seeing ~15% error rate on the public inference endpoint, spiking latency > 4s. Reporting to the customer now.
Tara (oncall): Action plan: 1) Quarantine nodes with highest retransmits from scheduler to reduce KV sync pressure, 2) Failover traffic to warm standby pool, 3) Neteng to throttle offending ports and investigate switch config, 4) Runtime to add transient OOM guard (temporary cgroup mem limit) to prevent container restarts while we stabilize.
Miguel (runtime): I can push a hotfix to the autoscaler to mark pods as degraded instead of immediate restart for OOMs coming after reconnect events. Deploy patch to canary group infer-canary-2 now.
Alice (sre): Tara — please cordon gpu-44 and gpu-45, drain gracefully. We'll evict pods to standby pool. Use: `kubectl cordon gpu-44 && kubectl drain gpu-44 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Tara (oncall): Doing that now. Cordoning gpu-44. Evicting pods, shifting traffic to standby.
ops-bot: deployment infer-routing updated: route weight shifted 70%->standby-pool, 30%->primary.
Ben (neteng): Temporarily disabled IB port 3/1 on switch sw-b-21 to stop retransmit storms. Monitoring for fab stability.
Miguel (runtime): Canary runtime patch applied. Added short-circuit so OOM after repeated KV reconnects will mark instance degraded and leakless-shutdown instead of immediate full restart.
Alice (sre): Observability note: kvcache miss surge drops from 2400/s -> 400/s after routing shift. CUDA OOMs stopped on nodes that were drained. One remaining node (gpu-43) still shows intermittent timeouts.
Tara (oncall): Ben — any ETA on fabric config rollback?
Ben (neteng): I'm coordinating with switch team. We spotted a misapplied QoS profile earlier today. Rolling back that change now, ETA ~12 minutes.
Jules (support): Customer notified: we opened a ticket and routed them to status; we're seeing degraded latency and intermittent errors. Will update once fabric rollback completes.
Miguel (runtime): FYI, adding a temporary kv-cache backoff in runtime config: `kvcache.max_retries=3` and `kvcache.reconnect_backoff_ms=2000` to reduce thundering reconns. Pushing to prod config.
Alice (sre): After rollback kicked in we see retransmit rates falling. Kernel timeouts on gpu-43 cleared. No new OOMs in last 4 minutes.
incident-bot: Incident state changed: P1 -> mitigated (partial). Postmortem required.
Tara (oncall): Live mitigation summary: cordoned 2 problematic nodes, shifted 70% traffic to standby, applied runtime degradations & backoffs, neteng rolled back QoS, disabled flapping port. Immediate customer impact reduced to <2% error rate.
Jules (support): Customer updated w/ mitigation note and ETA for full fix.
Ben (neteng): Leaving the port disabled until switch firmware checks complete and config validated, will report back with a changelog.
Miguel (runtime): I'll open a follow-up PR to make the transient OOM guard default for clusters with remote kvcache enabled. Also adding a metric for 'oom-after-reconnect' so we can alert earlier.
Alice (sre): Assigning postmortem: SRE + NetEng + Runtime. Action items: 1) Run fab-wide QoS audit, 2) Add kvcache backoff by default, 3) Improve routing fallback automation to cut traffic faster.
Tara (oncall): Thanks all. Putting incident into monitoring/resolved state for now. If errors spike again I'll re-pager immediately. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident closed at 2026-03-15T02:22:00Z (incident ID INC-20260315-1729). Postmortem assigned to @Alice (sre), @Ben (neteng), @Miguel (runtime).
